column1: How Exporters Neutralized an Increase in Tariffs

The thesis titled How Exporters Neutralized an Increase in Tariffs by Asier Minondo examines the response of Spanish exporters to unexpected tariff increases imposed by the US on European Union products due to the Airbus-Boeing conflict. The study utilizes firm-level data from Spain and employs a difference-in-differences methodology to assess the impact of these tariffs on export revenues. Despite the tariff hike  the export revenue of affected Spanish firms in the US did not significantly decrease compared to other Spanish exporters. The research identifies two primary strategies used by Spanish exporters to mitigate the impact of the tariffs: substituting Spanish products with those from countries not affected by the tariffs and shifting to product varieties not targeted by the tariffs. For instance  Spanish olive oil exporters increased imports from Tunisia and Portugal  bottling the oil in Spain and exporting it to the US as products of these countries  thus avoiding tariffs. Similarly  wine and cheese producers shifted exports to non-targeted varieties  such as exporting wines with higher alcohol content that were not subject to additional tariffs. The study concludes that tariff avoidance is a viable strategy for exporters to counteract tariff hikes  adding a new dimension to the ways firms can adjust to changes in trade policy. This research contributes to the literature on trade policy adjustment  highlighting the importance of trade avoidance as a strategy alongside traditional responses like reducing sales or exiting markets. The findings underscore the adaptability of exporters in the face of protectionist trade measures and provide insights into the broader implications of trade policy changes on international trade dynamics.
